findings.title: Historical audit JSON includes the local account name
findings.reproduction: Inspect the executed command arguments before shipping the audit record.
findings.observed: Ten command arguments contain the absolute local home path. Cargo lists this JSON among the files that the package would distribute.
findings.impact: Publishing the file discloses a local account name and workspace layout. No passwords or recovery material were identified in these references.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the prepared public edition with <audit-dir> paths and preserve the private original and its checksums locally.
findings.requiredVerification: Validated the proposed JSON against the report schema and checked all 19 historic command log digests. Apply it before publication.

findings.title: Published audit links lead to private logs and a missing checksum manifest
findings.reproduction: Resolve the fifteen links as they would appear in a Git checkout.
findings.expected: Public links lead to published files. Local evidence is identified and the minimal reproducer can be run.
findings.observed: Thirteen links target the ignored evidence directory. One links to an absent SHA256SUMS. The original independent fixture was under the ignored directory.
findings.impact: Readers cannot follow the advertised references or retrieve the reproduction from the public report.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the prepared public report and its small AUD-004-harnesses directory. Keep raw logs local.
findings.requiredVerification: All relative Markdown links in the prepared copy resolve within that copy.

findings.title: Release documentation omits the latest complete and targeted coverage results
findings.reproduction: Compare the documented 98.35% for its older source fingerprint with AUD-004 and the fresh DOC-09 measurement.
findings.expected: The README identifies the latest complete coverage result, and the details identify any newer, narrower measurement and its source.
findings.observed: The README still shows 98.35% for an older snapshot. The last complete Linux measurement was 97.23% (5,891 of 6,059 lines) for c2777f00 in AUD-004. The current measurement of 47 unit and seven strict integration tests covered 90.82% (5,533/6,092). Neither current release document contains those updated figures.
findings.impact: Readers using the release documents cannot see how much of the new strict file API was exercised. The old number remains a valid historical measurement.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the latest complete result in the README. In docs/COVERAGE.md, publish the full result and the current targeted result separately. Label the current per-file table with the targeted scope.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the previous complete result against AUD-004, and the targeted result against the current input fingerprint and per-file totals. The audit includes all file counts. A separate local coverage-only patch applied cleanly in git apply --check.

remediation.title: File metadata preserves the strict writer
remediation.evidence: src/strict/files.rs:48,97,120,132,151,162,183,249; src/strict.rs:119. Header, set facts and code remain strict types throughout. A protected input with a Vec destination produced precisely E0277 for HeldMut. Each independent probe had one invalid argument. With a protected destination the output matched the explicit portable writer.

remediation.title: Public geometry on platforms without a protected stack
remediation.evidence: README.md:237,296; docs/TECHNICAL.md:277,283; tests/suite/strict_elsewhere.rs:10. Public geometry and metadata remain usable. Calls that process payload bytes require a protected stack and refuse on Windows/WASM. Source and platform tests agree. This is not a new native Windows run.

remediation.title: Full equality includes the input binding
remediation.evidence: src/correct/changes.rs:207,325; docs/TECHNICAL.md:187; docs/audits/README.md:62. The docs distinguish matching locations and values from matching bound plans. Ordinary equality reads the words and the binding on the calling thread. strict::values remains the documented callback for a secret.

remediation.title: No implicit portable payload writer through strict file metadata
remediation.evidence: src/strict/files.rs:97,151,162,183,249; src/strict/codes.rs:42. The remaining gap in this finding is closed. The strict writer paths require Held/HeldMut, and a caller who wants portable writers must opt in. Returned payloads and explicit comparisons remain subject to the documented application contract.

limitations: Release candidate is uncommitted. GitHub’s Linux ARM64, macOS and Windows native CI for these source bytes is outstanding. CI is also required on the final Linux x86-64 revision. Local Linux checks and target cross-lints cannot replace native checks. The configured native matrix does not cover Android or iOS device execution.

Author feature-matrix and five fuzz runs were inspected and retained. Only the negative doctest input changed between those runs and the final handoff. The final doctests and independent API probes were executed separately.
cargo audit used the locally cached RustSec advisory database. Fresh advisory lookup on the release commit belongs to CI.

The manifest intentionally disables crates.io publication while the format is marked draft. The package contents listing and an offline dry run were checked. No publishable archive was certified, and reproducible release packaging and signatures were not tested.

The full instrumented suite timed out after 35 minutes (exit 124). A broader retry exited 143 with an empty log. The current Linux x86-64 default-feature coverage uses the completed unit stage (47 tests) and fresh profiles for seven strict integration tests. The ordinary suite passed all 165 integration tests. Coverage from the other 158 integration tests contributes nothing to the current figure. Coverage excludes test sources, doctests, fuzz campaigns, the separate field proof, other platforms and feature sets. The latest complete result is 97.23% (5,891 of 6,059 lines) for snapshot c2777f00.

Existing strict-mode limits include OS-specific memory properties, caller-owned copies after return and ordinary equality on returned plans. The legacy AUD-002-SEC001 native acceptance requirement is distinct from the four findings verified here.
